chapter_title: Concerning the Fifteen Paths; and whether the Catechumen would have avoided causing his Wealth to go on the Three Paths to Gehenna
chapter_note: Heavily institutional chapter. The only substrate is the cosmological teaching about the fifteen paths in the zone (¶2-4), which the elect recaps as background to an institutional question about catechumen soteriology. The recapped teaching — fifteen paths (4 pure/8 mixed/3 waste), the three waste paths enumerated, and the cosmic law that persons follow their deeds — is genuine substrate cosmology (zone architecture, ships, light-waste separation, Cross of Light). Everything from ¶5 onward is institutional ecclesiology: how apostles pre-choose forms of their church, the seal of faith protecting catechumens, fasting/prayer purifying pre-conversion deeds, and an extended analogy about deeds traveling at different speeds. Gardner notes Buddhist karmic influence, thoroughly integrated into Manichaean institutional framework. Teaching purity 0.289 confirms institutional dominance.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure dialogue frame formula: 'Once again, an elect stood up before the apostle' + 'I beseech you, my master' honorific. No cosmological content.

paragraphs.core_text: Fifteen paths are drawn out in the zone. Four paths are pure and belong [to the] light, leading up to life. Eight other paths are [mixed], leading above from that place. The light shall go [u]p and become free through them; be purified and go in [to the] ships. However, the waste is separated and thrown [dow]n to transmigr[a]tion and the other three paths of [waste ...] discharged to the gehennas.
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped citation frame 'For we have heard thus from you:' — elect quoting back prior teaching.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core substrate cosmology: systematic zone architecture mapping fifteen paths to three categories (pure/mixed/waste). Both sides stay within cosmic system — zone, paths, light, ships, waste, transmigration, gehennas. The 4/8/3 structure is a classic numerical-correspondential teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: [The three] paths that belong to waste, the ones that are drawn to the gehennas, [a]re drawn from the fleshes. O[n]e of them is the appetite for [lawl]essness, that of people and of all flesh. The second is the [ ... ] all bodies, which is slaughter, [with] which all flesh is consumed. The third is the damaging action, which [ ... ] the Cross of Light and every body; together with the rest of the error and the blasphemy that wounds the gods.
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped 'You have explained [that' — citation formula referencing prior teaching. Adjusted opening to preserve restoration brackets on '[the three]'.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Three-fold enumeration of waste paths: appetite/slaughter/damaging action. Cross of Light and 'wounds the gods' are cosmic entities as agents. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. Enumeration markers ('One of them', 'The second', 'The third') preserved as structural substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Th[ese th]ree paths lead to the gehennas. Every person shall follow after hi[s] de[e]ds, whether to life or indeed to death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped 'have you taught us, that they' and 'And you have also [told] us that' — citation frame formulas.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Two substrate principles recapitulated: (1) three paths lead to gehennas, (2) universal cosmic law that persons follow their deeds. The second principle is a fundamental cosmological-moral law expressed impersonally. Substrate score 8.82 reflects high cosmic vocabulary density in short paragraph.

The elect's question pivots from cosmic categories to institutional soteriology: 'the lesson of the catechumen,' 'before he receives the faith of God.' The three paths are re-enumerated (appetite in bones, appetite of fornication, damaging action) but entirely in service of asking about the catechumen's institutional fate. Institutional score 8.7.

Continuation of institutional question. 'Before he becomes a catechumen,' 'receive the faith of God,' 'multitude of catechumens set in the world.' The cosmic vocabulary (gehennas, transmigration) is entirely subordinated to the institutional question about catechumen salvation.
Pure dialogue frame transition: 'Then the apostle speaks to that elect' + 'I am the one who will enlighten you.' No teaching content.

Editorial seam detected. 'Now, this is how it is for you to understand' is a bridge connective introducing institutional ecclesiology: apostle pre-choosing forms of 'his entire church,' elect and catechumens. The concept of pre-chosen heavenly forms has cosmological resonance but is deployed entirely for institutional soteriology — explaining how the apostle's church is predetermined.

Probable editorial extension flagged. 'Various sects and heresies,' 'error of the sects,' 'seal of the faith and the knowledge' — institutional vocabulary throughout. The angels guiding deeds to purification serves the institutional argument. 'Light word' is the only cosmic element but it's in service of the apostle's converting activity.
Illustrative analogy: royal horse with king's seal = catechumen with faith's seal. Mundane parable serving institutional argument. No cosmic vocabulary or systematic mapping.

Institutional soteriology: catechumen's form chosen from the start protects deeds from gehennas. 'Form established above in the heights' uses cosmic geography in service of institutional pre-election doctrine. The argument structure — former works protected like latter works — is institutional logic about conversion timing.

Institutional practices listed: fasting, prayer, alms given to the saints. Deeds drawn to transmigrations rather than gehennas, then purified by angels — institutional soteriology. 'New deeds' as 'nullifier of first deeds' is the institutional answer to the catechumen question.

Probable editorial extension flagged. Institutional vocabulary dense: 'right hand of peace,' 'rank of the true catechumenate,' 'grace,' 'first fasts.' Contains cosmic process language ('loosen their bond and ascend from heaven and earth, from the trees and the fleshes,' 'light ship of the night') but this is substrate vocabulary thoroughly absorbed into institutional soteriology — the cosmic process is triggered by institutional practice (fasting/prayer). Cannot cleanly extract substrate without destroying the institutional argument.
Institutional conclusion about catechumen's ability to free deeds 'by his own hand, while being in his body.' Institutional soteriology about the efficacy of the catechumen's practice.

Extended analogy: king dwelling in a city with his following scattered in surrounding dwellings, then giving sign for departure. All vocabulary scores zero — neutral parable language. Serves the institutional teaching about how deeds travel at different speeds. Gardner notes Buddhist karmic influence on this section.

Continuation of king's-host analogy: three groups travel before/with/after the king. This three-fold temporal pattern (preceding/accompanying/following) structures the institutional teaching in ¶18. All vocabulary scores zero.
Summary of analogy: following departs at different times, not all at once. Brief recapitulation preparing for the application in ¶18.

Application of analogy to catechumen's deeds: some purified while in body, some freed at death, some freed afterward from 'bonds of the earth and that of the creatures.' Contains cosmic geography vocabulary ('firmaments of the heavens,' 'land of the living,' 'bonds of the earth') but deployed entirely for institutional catechumen soteriology.

Concluding summary: 'I have instructed you about the catechumen.' Institutional closure. 'Land of the living' is cosmic geography absorbed into institutional vocabulary. 'Angels hasten' continues the institutional mechanism of catechumen protection.
